# Assurance capability matrix

<!-- generated by scripts/render-assurance-docs.mjs; do not edit by hand. Regenerate with `npm run docs:assurance` in scanner/. -->

Scope of the verification, deployment, invariant and capability-enforcement features, read from the code that implements them. A cell says what the repository has executed, not what it hopes to support. "Supported" for a platform means the repository's own tests were executed there; "unverified" means no outcome is claimed; "unsupported" means the feature refuses to run. Every feature below is off by default and the high-risk ones are operator-only.

## Features, risk class and platforms

| Feature | Risk class | Platforms where it can run at all | Platform note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `verification-oracles` | high-risk-execution | linux, darwin | runtime oracles run through the confinement sandbox; isolation-required checks are only advertised on Linux |
| `patch-negative-verification` | high-risk-execution | linux, darwin | replays the exploit against the original and the patched revision through the confinement sandbox, so it needs verification-oracles as well; an unproved isolation control blocks it |
| `deployment-boundaries` | passive | linux, darwin, win32 | none |
| `invariant-scenarios` | high-risk-execution | linux, darwin | stateful scenarios execute target code and need the confinement sandbox |
| `capability-enforcement` | high-risk-execution | linux | runner-level filesystem, network and process enforcement is only advertised on Linux; macOS can supervise but not enforce |
| `model-routing` | model-network | linux, darwin, win32 | none |
| `portfolio-assurance` | passive | linux, darwin, win32 | none |

## Runtime oracles: class, prerequisites and platform status

Oracle targets are small JavaScript modules run under Node (the `node-runtime` prerequisite) inside the trust boundary. That is the whole language scope of the oracles: detector support for the nine core languages and for Haskell and Nix is a separate matter, listed in [language support](../language-support.md), and detector support alone does not imply oracle support. An unmet prerequisite is reported `unsupported` and the target never runs.

### Non-taint vulnerability classes

| Class | Executed by | Claim it can test | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tenant-authorization` | `authorization-decision` | an actor from one tenant is allowed to read or change another tenant's resource | [fixtures](../../scanner/test/fixtures/non-taint/tenant-authorization) |
| `privileged-action` | `authorization-decision` | a lower-privileged actor is allowed to perform an action reserved for a higher role | [fixtures](../../scanner/test/fixtures/non-taint/privileged-action) |
| `workflow-order` | `state-transition` | a step that must follow another can be performed first (for example a refund before approval) | [fixtures](../../scanner/test/fixtures/non-taint/workflow-order) |
| `replay-idempotency` | `replay-idempotency` | delivering the same request again repeats its side effect (a double charge, a double credit) | [fixtures](../../scanner/test/fixtures/non-taint/replay-idempotency) |
| `resource-exhaustion` | `parser-resource` | a bounded hostile parameter makes the code exceed its time or output budget (an uncapped page size, an unbounded loop) | [fixtures](../../scanner/test/fixtures/non-taint/resource-exhaustion) |

Named as unsupported, with the reason:

| Class | CWEs | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `concurrent-race` | CWE-362, CWE-367 | a race needs concurrent scheduling; the adapters deliver sequentially, so no verdict about a race can be formed |
| `cross-site-request-forgery` | CWE-352 | needs a browser and a session; no adapter exercises one |
| `authentication-throttling` | CWE-307, CWE-799 | needs a stateful attempt counter over time and a populated store; the adapters bound a single input, not a campaign |

## Deployment adapters

An adapter is validated for deployment-aware claims only when the frozen synthetic ablation holds a positive and a negative fixture for it and no baseline defect was lost. The status column is read from the validated-adapters table in [deployment-aware support](../guides/deployment-aware-support.md), which a test compares with the evaluation itself.

| Adapter | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `kubernetes` | validated |
| `compose` | validated |
| `terraform-plan` | not validated |
| `iam-policy` | not validated |

## Invariants: classes, scenario kinds and bounds

| Invariant class | Scenario kinds generated |
| --- | --- |
| `tenant-isolation` | `cross-tenant-access` |
| `privilege-constraint` | `privilege-change` |
| `value-conservation` | `duplicate-request`, `concurrent-operations` |
| `workflow-order` | `reordered-workflow` |
| `idempotency` | `duplicate-request`, `concurrent-operations` |

Hard bounds on a generated scenario (a request over a ceiling is rejected, not clamped): `actors` 4, `depth` 12, `requests` 16, `scenarios` 6, `timeBudgetMs` 8000. Contract document limits: `actors` 8, `tenants` 4, `resources` 16, `transitions` 24, `forbidden` 8.

Limits of the invariant tooling, as the guide states them: the application is a factory over an in-memory store (durable state in a real database, queue or file system is not observed); concurrency is cooperative scheduling in one process; a clean result covers only the declared bounded scenarios; a proposed or inferred contract is advisory until a named human approves it. See [business-logic invariants](../guides/business-logic-invariants.md).

## Enforced-capability backend

| Platform | Backend | Status | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| linux | namespace | `unverified` | advertised for enforced mode, but the control probes in this module have not run on a Linux host from this workspace. Several controls are not implemented on the namespace backend (read confinement to declared roots, several write roots, mediated network, supervised tree termination), so enforced mode is blocked there until they are implemented and the sandbox-linux job shows them proved. Process-count caps are never claimed. |
| darwin | userspace | `host-proved-not-advertised` | the active probes can prove the controls on a macOS host, and tasks can run there for development only when the caller opts in; macOS is not an advertised enforced backend. |
| win32 | none | `unsupported` | no isolation backend exists on Windows. |

Controls proved by active probes before an enforced task runs: `fs-read-confinement`, `fs-multi-root-write`, `network-mediation`. An enforced task is released only on an advertised backend with every control it depends on proved; a control that is not proved blocks the run and the target never executes.

Standing limitations, stated in every capability report:

- Top-level executables and arguments are mediated. A descendant inherits file and network confinement and is terminated with the task, but its own exec calls are not allowlisted.
- Metadata of the ancestors of a declared root is visible; the existence and size of other paths are not.
- HTTPS is an opaque tunnel to a declared destination: its payload is not inspected. Plaintext HTTP is filtered for secrets before it is forwarded.
- The mediation proxy accepts connections from any local process. It only forwards to declared destinations, so the exposure is the declared set.
- A process that double-forks and calls setsid between two supervisor sweeps can outlive the task; only a PID namespace or cgroup closes that gap.
- Process-count caps are per-user and system-wide on the host and did not refuse on a hosted Linux runner in a previous release; none is claimed enforced on any backend.
- Address-space (memory) caps are not enforceable on macOS and are carried, not enforced.
